paragraphs.name: 3ba5
paragraphs.text: 2018 article follows:

paragraphs.name: 43b2
paragraphs.text: A year ago, we wrote about Getting Singapore making with micro:bit and the Digital Maker Programme. Since then, we’ve been busy creating new micro:bit kits and writing tutorials for our micro:bit Tinker Kit— and we’ll tell you more about these soon!—but here’s an exciting project we’ve been working on: designing our very own micro:bit competition.

paragraphs.name: 098c
paragraphs.text: For this year’s National Infocomm Challenge, we wanted to do something different from the “usual” micro:bit hackathon. So, for the inaugural version of this micro:bit competition in Singapore, participants will create their own game controllers to play a capture-the-flag style video game we made, called Tank Tinkerer:

paragraphs.name: 99b0
paragraphs.text: “ALL KINDS OF WEIRD SHENANIGANS”

paragraphs.name: 8af6
paragraphs.text: (And yes, it’s called Tank Tinkerer because that’s an anagram of our company name. We felt clever for days after coming up with this.)

paragraphs.name: e090
paragraphs.text: This is the official competition website, just for info, because registration has closed and we’re on to the finals soon:

paragraphs.name: e985
paragraphs.text:
Digital Making National Infocomm Challenge - Tinkercademy
Tinkercademy is proud to present, in collaboration with 3D Tronics and the IMDA Digital Maker Programme, the Senior…tinkercademy.com

paragraphs.name: 31b5
paragraphs.text: At time of writing, we’ve reviewed 60+ teams in the preliminaries, and are looking forward to the finals at Tech Saturday this weekend (2 June, 10am) at Suntec City. We’ll share pictures and videos on our social media (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram), and we’ll hopefully have our very talented young intern Jerrayl write about his experience creating the game in Unity.

paragraphs.name: a3ca
paragraphs.text: In the meantime, we’d like to share a bit more about the competition: what is Tank Tinkerer, how is Tank Tinkerer played, and (with apologies to one green-skinned Guardian), why is Tank Tinkerer.
What is Tank Tinkerer?

paragraphs.name: 75b2
paragraphs.text: The game itself is available for download from itch.io, linked below.

paragraphs.name: 20af
paragraphs.text:
Tank Tinkerer by tinkercademy
The official competition game for the 3d-tronics Digital Making Infocomm Challenge 2018! Available for Windows, macOStinkercademy.itch.io

paragraphs.name: debe
paragraphs.text: What do participants actually do in this competition? The simple answer: Design micro:bit controllers that send wireless signals to control their tanks in the Tank Tinkerer game.

paragraphs.name: fc04
paragraphs.text: What we hope participants do, though, is to make the controllers be as visually striking as possible. As such, we’re hoping for entries such as giant cardboard constructions, DIY craft props, a co-ordinated dance sequence, and/or lots and lots of wild, flailing limb movements.

paragraphs.name: f8a9
paragraphs.text: Example controller 1

paragraphs.name: 814f
paragraphs.text: Example controller 2

paragraphs.name: f709
paragraphs.text: How does Tank Tinkerer work?

paragraphs.name: be1b
paragraphs.text: We (well… mostly Jerrayl) made the game in Unity, out of a variety of open-source models and prefabs—you can grab a copy of the source code here:

paragraphs.name: 9abd
paragraphs.text:
Tinkertanker/TankTinkerer
TankTinkerer Gamegithub.com

paragraphs.name: 24f4
paragraphs.text: Aside: Look at that URL! Tinkertanker/TankTinkerer! Ahha haaha haha! Oh, ahem, sorry.

paragraphs.name: 69b2
paragraphs.text: How do controllers talk to the game? The Tank Tinkerer game reads serial input from a receiver micro:bit, connected to the game computer by USB. The micro:bit controllers, or senders, simply send keyboard commands (e.g. W to move forward, S to move back) to the received to control the game. Our installation guide has information anyone needs to get the game set up properly.

paragraphs.name: 589c
paragraphs.text: Won’t participants experience lots of lag time by having to send their controls over the micro:bit radio? Yes. This is intentional, and also hilarious to watch.

paragraphs.name: 2b85
paragraphs.text: How do participants win? We split the competition into two main categories, with prizes for the top controller designs, and a 64-team tournament for the best players. We’re also hoping to see some teams dress up for the Best Theme.
Why this competition?

paragraphs.name: 11b0
paragraphs.text: When designing this competition, we were heavily inspired by the Nintendo LABO launch video from earlier this year:

paragraphs.name: f8e0
paragraphs.text: By having the competition be about designing game controllers, we aim to have participants create physical, real-world objects that interact with our game’s virtual world. We think this is a great way to bring together maker concepts such as sensors & actuators, inter-device connectivity, and even a dash of augmented reality, to excite participants into thinking up their next great connected device project.

paragraphs.name: 3e81
paragraphs.text: Many Tanks To…

paragraphs.name: e87b
paragraphs.text: Our competition partners Zenitant for all their invaluable assistance in organising the competition, and registering and co-ordinating with schools; the Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore for making the Digital Maker Programme happen; and the Methodist Girls’ School Infocomm Club for their critical support and play-testing in the game’s early development.

paragraphs.name: da3f
paragraphs.text: Want to run your own?

Are you interested in running a Tank Tinkerer competition in your school, district, or country? All the source code and executables are free to use! Just please drop us an email so we know where this ends up, if you really need some help setting up, or if you have improvements to make.
